text:
Alice: Hi — following the quickstart curl example and I'm getting 401 invalid_api_key when calling /v1/chat/completions. Anyone seen this?
Nina (Support): Can you paste the exact curl you ran (sanitized key ok)? Also the full response body if available.
Alice: sure, here's what I used (removed my real key):
```
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Api-Key <sk-test-ABc123...>" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-small","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'
```
Alice: Response: {"error":{"type":"invalid_api_key","message":"401 Unauthorized"}}
Sam (Dev): ahhh. You included the angle brackets around the key. The docs show <API_KEY> as a placeholder and folks sometimes copy that literally.
Nina (Support): Yep — the header should be exactly the key, no surrounding < > or quotes. Try `-H "Authorization: Api-Key sk-test-ABc123..."` instead.
Alice: trying now...
DeployBot: [deploy-log] request_id=req-0a1b2c status=401 path=/v1/chat/completions
Alice: OK that worked after removing the brackets — 200 and reply received. Thanks!
Sam (Dev): Also watch for accidental surrounding quotes if you export the key as a shell var like `export REDWOOD_API_KEY='"sk-..."'` — that will include quotes.
Nina (Support): Glad it's fixed. I'll add a tiny note to the quickstart to avoid angle-bracket confusion. :thumbsup:
Alice: :thumbsup:
